# `aitbc market escrow create`

Create an on-chain escrow for a job with buyer, provider, and optional amount.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc market escrow create [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--job-id` | text | — | yes | Coordinator job ID. |
| `--buyer` | text | — | yes | The Buyer. |
| `--provider` | text | — | yes | The Provider. |
| `--amount` | decimal | — | no | Amount of AIT. |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet name to sign the escrow lock |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc market escrow create --job-id <job_id> --buyer <buyer> --provider <provider>
```
